items.title: Jeff Riddick Interview, 1983-07-14
items.q: And Ellen was dancing in that line. And we fell in love in April and married in August

ctx.x: Uh huh. Dewey Luke, Cy Million, all of those fellas banked this Alfred Hirsch, one of the most prominent men in that part of the country. Uh huh. And very rich, a multi-millionaire owned the Tivoli Club. Uh huh. And we were the first band that played there. In about five months or something like that, we got this offer to go on the road with this unit that was leaving the Sanger Theater for the summer. In that unit was six girls in a line. It was no burlesque or nothing like that. It was just strictly a tab,…

items.title: Jeff Riddick Interview, 1983-08-01
items.q: However, Ellen drove the car home.

ctx.x: How about on the road if you wanted to drink? And this was during Prohibition. Was it hard to find a drink?

Very much so until you got to where you were playing. And when you started to play that night, as a general rule, the guy that ran the dance brought you a quart of whiskey. And it would knock your head off. Sometimes 110 proof alcohol. Call it white lightning or mountain dew. It's all according to where you were. Up in Tennessee, they called it mountain dew. Mississippi, they called it white lightning. Sometimes we'd be on the road and drinking out of a fruit jar. I got a scar across the bridge of my nose now…
